deck: Table Rock this morning: 910.46 ft. Taneycomo still eats on a pink worm if the generators give you a window.

play.title: Fish the wind.
play.body: Fall bass set up where the shad get blown. A crankbait that bangs is better than a worm that sits.

season.name: Fall turnover
season.why: The lake turns over and the fish don't read the same book they did in August. Crankbaits get good again. Trout streamers get good. This is the season Branson locals wait for.
tips: Windblown banks and shad-colored cranks, 8–18 feet.
Walleye on the same gravel they used all summer, just shallower.
Taneycomo: streamers and wooly buggers when they generate. Hoppers until the first frost.
A jacket in the boat. Dawn is cold before the strip is.

weekGraf: Table Rock held near 910.46 ft all week, a hair under full pool (915). 1 morning this week the desk had no new gage (carry-forward). Numbers marked “desk” were read from that day’s scout; “carry” was not. Ramps are still in. Shallow coves feel a falling pool first.

now.clarity: Clear near the dam; arms can stain. Verify locally.

body: At 910.46 ft the lake is showing plenty of bank and structure that stays hidden at higher pools. Stumps and laydowns in the creek arms and coves are closer to the surface — run slow and watch your depthfinder. Clarity is excellent.

Bass have moved off the shallow flats. Look for them on long points, gravel transitions that drop into 20-35 feet, and around offshore brush. Jigs, drop-shots, and lipless crankbaits are producing when presented cleanly. The cooling water is pushing fish deeper each day. Walleye and crappie reports remain steady around docks and deeper brush piles.

taneycomo.dek: Cold tailwater · generation is the whole game

now.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F below the dam). Verify at the bank.
now.generation: ~298 cfs on the last printed reading. Not a live hourly. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

body: Cold releases from the bottom of Table Rock keep this tailwater in the mid-55s even as air temperatures drop. Generation is the entire playbook: low water this morning opens wading and light-line drifting or indicator fishing. When the turbines ramp up, the current stacks fish in the eddies and seams and you need weight to get down.

From Table Rock Dam downstream to Fall Creek it is artificial lures and flies only — no soft plastics, no scented baits, no natural bait. Rainbows 12–20 inches must be released. Below Fall Creek you can fish pink worms, PowerBait, or other scented options. Micro jigs, midges, scuds, and small streamers are working. Call SWPA at 866-494-1993 before you go so you don't get surprised by rising water.
